question: neo-ssd is idle with nothing queued, so it has 360 minutes; real-psample costs 8 minutes per sample. In LC3, rsync with eager writeback beat default xs, while xs-eager was much faster than xs. No experiment has put xs-eager against rsync-eager directly, and that comparison decides whether xs can beat rsync on this local copy. LC4 reported only the no-op cell, so the 1% update re-sync is still open. The eager plus --no-atomic combination has not been tried. The waiting tree confirmation of xs-eager against plain xs (LC3-durable-confirm) is left to the T14 tree, so it is not duplicated here. Budget: 96 minutes of screening plus 128 if the confirmation runs, then 64 and 64, about 352 minutes in total.

nodes.question: When both tools flush eagerly, does xs -aH get the psample backup safely onto the T5 sooner than rsync -aH?
nodes.hypothesis: With eager writeback on both sides, xs -aH reaches a durable copy of psample on the T5 at least 5% sooner than rsync -aH. LC3's screening implies a time ratio near 0.77.
not clearly faster: the next window's plan reads this

nodes.question: Does xs-eager hold up on 8 fresh blocks?
nodes.hypothesis: Confirms the fastest arm of N0 with 8 fresh blocks, if it had one.

nodes.question: After 1% of the psample files change, does xs -aH re-sync the local T5 backup faster than rsync -aH with cold caches?
nodes.hypothesis: xs -aH finishes the 1% update re-sync of psample onto the T5 faster than rsync -aH, as it did for the no-op re-sync (time ratio 0.52).

nodes.question: Does skipping the temp-file rename add any speed on top of eager writeback for the local psample backup?
nodes.hypothesis: Adding --no-atomic to xs -aH with eager writeback makes the durable psample copy to the T5 at least 5% faster than eager writeback alone.
